speaker: narrator
text: What if a *solar storm* hit tonight?

speaker: narrator
text: Friday, four p.m. Jay is fixing his *bike*.

speaker: narrator
text: Bit is watching the Sun. Bit *always* watches.

speaker: narrator
text: Then Bit goes *quiet*.

speaker: bit
text: Jay. The Sun just *exploded*. A little.

speaker: bit
text: A flare. And a cloud of *magnetic plasma*.

speaker: bit
text: It's coming *here*.

speaker: hero
text: Okay. Is that *bad*?

speaker: bit
text: It happened once before. *Eighteen fifty nine*.

speaker: bit
text: A man named Carrington *saw* the flare.

speaker: bit
text: Seventeen and a half hours *later*, it hit.

speaker: bit
text: The sky glowed red and green. Even over *Mexico*.

speaker: bit
text: Telegraph wires threw *sparks*.

speaker: hero
text: That was wires. We have *phones* now.

speaker: bit
text: Jay. Today *everything* is wires.

speaker: bit
text: Power grids. Satellites. GPS. Your phone. *Me*.

speaker: narrator
text: Bit puts a timer in the *corner*.

speaker: hero
text: Then we warn everyone. You'll *help*, right?

speaker: narrator
text: Bit doesn't answer *right away*.

speaker: bit
text: Jay. I'm *made* of electricity too.

speaker: bit
text: Before it hits, I have to turn myself *off*.

speaker: hero
text: Off? For how *long*?

speaker: bit
text: Until it's over. A day. *Maybe two*.

speaker: narrator
text: Jay has never spent *one hour* without Bit.

speaker: narrator
text: Seven p.m. Town hall. Mayor Doyle *laughs*.

speaker: boss
text: A storm from the *Sun*? It's sunny!

speaker: narrator
text: Only Grandpa Ezra stands *up*.

speaker: scientist
text: I was a railway *telegraph* man. Forty years.

speaker: scientist
text: The boy's robot is *right*. Unplug everything.

speaker: narrator
text: Bit makes a list. Jay reads it *out loud*.

speaker: narrator
text: Nia fills her bakery with *candles*.

speaker: narrator
text: Her brother Milo is *thrilled*.

speaker: kid
text: Northern lights? *Here*? I'm staying up!

speaker: narrator
text: Ezra teaches Milo one thing. *Morse code*.

speaker: kid
text: Beep beep beep. *Boop boop boop*.

speaker: narrator
text: Three a.m. One hour *left*.

speaker: bit
text: Jay. You'll be fine. You were fine *before* me.

speaker: hero
text: I don't *remember* before you.

speaker: bit
text: Goodnight, Jay. Look up for *me*.

speaker: narrator
text: And for the first time ever, Bit goes *dark*.

speaker: narrator
text: Four a.m. Jay steps *outside*.

speaker: narrator
text: At first, *nothing*.

speaker: narrator
text: Then the sky turns *green*.

speaker: narrator
text: Then *red*. Then purple. Moving like *curtains*.

speaker: kid
text: *Wooow*. Nia! NIA! Come *look*!

speaker: narrator
text: Somewhere, a dog howls at the *sky*.

speaker: narrator
text: Every streetlight in town *flickers*.

speaker: narrator
text: Then the whole town goes *dark*.

speaker: narrator
text: Phones: no signal. No GPS. No *internet*.

speaker: narrator
text: But it isn't dark. The sky is *glowing*.

speaker: narrator
text: Nia unfolds a newspaper. She can *read* it.

speaker: hero
text: Bit said that happened in *eighteen fifty nine*.

speaker: narrator
text: Down the street, a light comes on at *Ezra's*.

speaker: narrator
text: Ezra is cooking *breakfast*.

speaker: scientist
text: It's bright. So it's *morning*. Eggs?

speaker: narrator
text: In 1859, gold miners did the *same thing*.

speaker: scientist
text: What? Nobody wants *eggs*?

speaker: narrator
text: Everyone laughs. For a *minute*.

speaker: narrator
text: Jay looks at Bit's dark screen. He *misses* him.

speaker: narrator
text: Then Nia *stops* laughing.

speaker: friend
text: Where's *Milo*?

speaker: narrator
text: Nia calls Milo. Nothing. The phones are *dead*.

speaker: narrator
text: Jay grabs his phone. *Bit, find Milo*.

speaker: narrator
text: Bit is *off*. Jay forgot.

speaker: hero
text: I don't know how to find *anyone* without Bit.

speaker: scientist
text: Then we find him the *old way*.

speaker: narrator
text: Ezra unfolds a paper map. Jay's never *used* one.

speaker: hero
text: Which way is *up*?

speaker: scientist
text: North. Where the lights are *brightest*.

speaker: friend
text: Milo said he wanted the *best view*.

speaker: hero
text: Mill Hill. The highest point in *town*.

speaker: narrator
text: Mill Hill is two miles away. In the *dark*.

speaker: narrator
text: No streetlights. No car *radio*. No Bit.

speaker: narrator
text: The old railway runs along the *road*.

speaker: narrator
text: Above it, the old telegraph wire is *humming*.

speaker: narrator
text: Ezra puts a hand near it. *Snap*!

speaker: scientist
text: Ha! It's *alive*. Just like the stories.

speaker: hero
text: Ezra, careful! That wire has no *power*!

speaker: scientist
text: It does tonight. The *sky* is the battery.

speaker: narrator
text: The old station. Ezra kicks the door *open*.

speaker: narrator
text: On the desk, a brass telegraph *key*.

speaker: scientist
text: In 1859, operators *unplugged* their batteries.

speaker: scientist
text: And kept sending. On the storm's power *alone*.

speaker: hero
text: Wait. That's *real*?

speaker: scientist
text: Real. Some got *shocks* too. Gloves.

speaker: narrator
text: The line runs to a hut on *Mill Hill*.

speaker: friend
text: If Milo's up there, would he *hear* it?

speaker: scientist
text: The hut has a sounder. It *clicks*. Loud.

speaker: narrator
text: Ezra's hands shake. He's eighty-one.

speaker: scientist
text: Jay. You *tap*. I'll spell.

speaker: narrator
text: Jay puts his finger on the key. *Click*.

speaker: narrator
text: A spark *jumps*. Jay doesn't let go.

speaker: narrator
text: Dot dot dot. Dash dash dash. *Dot dot dot*.

speaker: narrator
text: Again. And *again*.

speaker: scientist
text: Good. Slow. Like a *heartbeat*.

speaker: narrator
text: Five minutes. *Nothing*.

speaker: friend
text: He's not there. He's *not* there.

speaker: narrator
text: Then the sounder on the desk goes *click*.

speaker: narrator
text: Click. Click. *Click*.

speaker: scientist
text: That's not random. That's *Morse*.

speaker: narrator
text: Ezra writes each letter on the *wall*.

speaker: friend
text: Milo. It's *Milo*! He remembered!

speaker: scientist
text: One lesson. One. That boy is a *natural*.

speaker: narrator
text: Nia is already running for the *door*.

speaker: narrator
text: Jay follows her. Up Mill Hill. Under the *lights*.

speaker: friend
text: You're quiet. You're *never* quiet.

speaker: hero
text: When I'm scared, Bit tells me what to *do*.

speaker: hero
text: Tonight there's no Bit. Just *me*.

speaker: friend
text: Jay. *You* tapped that key. Not Bit.

speaker: narrator
text: At the top, a small shape in a *blanket*.

speaker: kid
text: Nia! I tapped back! Did you *hear* me?

speaker: narrator
text: Nia hugs him so hard he *squeaks*.

speaker: narrator
text: For a minute, all three just look *up*.

speaker: hero
text: Bit said look up for him. I'm *looking*.

speaker: narrator
text: Then Milo says something that makes Jay *freeze*.

speaker: kid
text: I charged my tablet. On *Bit's* dock.

speaker: hero
text: The dock is plugged *into the wall*.

speaker: narrator
text: If power comes back, the surge hits *Bit*.

speaker: narrator
text: Down the hill, the town lights *blink*.

speaker: friend
text: They're turning the power *back on*!

speaker: narrator
text: Jay runs. Two miles. *Downhill*.

speaker: narrator
text: His legs burn. His lungs burn. He *keeps going*.

speaker: narrator
text: Mayor Doyle is at the town *switch*.

speaker: boss
text: Storm's over! Lights in three, two...

speaker: narrator
text: The sky flares red *again*.

speaker: narrator
text: A second wave. Storms like this come in *pieces*.

speaker: narrator
text: Jay bursts through his door. The dock is *humming*.

speaker: narrator
text: He grabs the cable. *Pulls*.

speaker: narrator
text: A spark. A bang. Then the street goes *dark*.

speaker: narrator
text: The town transformer is *fried*.

speaker: narrator
text: No power for *three days*. That's the cost.

speaker: narrator
text: But the cable is in Jay's *hand*.

speaker: narrator
text: Morning. The sky is *blue* again.

speaker: narrator
text: Jay presses Bit's power button. *Nothing*.

speaker: narrator
text: Jay presses it again. And *again*.

speaker: hero
text: You said one day. Maybe *two*.

speaker: narrator
text: Ezra knocks. He holds up a *battery*. It's dead.

speaker: narrator
text: Every battery in town is *dead*.

speaker: narrator
text: Then Milo walks in. With a *solar panel*.

speaker: kid
text: It runs on the Sun. Is that *funny*?

speaker: narrator
text: The Sun broke Bit. Can the Sun *fix* him?

speaker: narrator
text: One hour. Two. Then a *beep*.

speaker: bit
text: Jay? Did you *look up*?

speaker: hero
text: Bit! I looked up. I used a *map*!

speaker: hero
text: And I sent Morse code. On a *storm*.

speaker: bit
text: Without me? I'm *proud*. And a bit jealous.

speaker: bit
text: Fun fact. In 2012, one *missed* us.

speaker: bit
text: By about *nine days*.

speaker: hero
text: Bit. Teach me *everything*. Just in case.

speaker: bit
text: Lesson one. *Unplug the dock*.

speaker: narrator
text: That night, the whole town *looks up*.

speaker: narrator
text: No storm. Just stars. And one robot *beeping*.

speaker: kid
text: Bit's doing Morse! It says... *T-H-A-N-K-S*.

speaker: narrator
text: Follow for a new What if every day.
